solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so we take the start of government

parts.note: a reedy voice is thin and shrill, like a reed instrument

explanation.surface: A grasping head of government with a piercing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacious means grasping and covetous, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Antelope starts to get nervous, uneasy

indicators.note: starts to points to the initial letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: An antelope becoming jittery, as prey animals do.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest is an African antelope, also called a gnu.

clue.text: Only part of a book, but containing relevant introduction

indicators.note: containing says the word for but holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: but in the sense 'all but' means except

indicators.note: introduction means just the first letter of relevant

explanation.surface: A reviewer quotes just part of a book, but includes the relevant introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage extracted from a longer text is only a portion of it.

clue.text: March day in Dorset ain't bad

indicators.note: in places the day inside the rearranged letters
bad suggests something wrong, so the letters of Dorset ain't are rearranged

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A complaint that a day in Dorset, an English county, isn't bad in March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is a protest; 'bad' is the anagram signal and 'in' puts the day inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is a public demonstration.

clue.text: Funny thing adding yellowish-white to scarlet, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word scarlet

parts.note: cream is the colour name for a pale yellowish-white

explanation.surface: Reads like a painter's instruction for mixing colours on a palette.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a hilarious person or thing is called a scream.

clue.text: Formal kit sold as cricket bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A shop advert: formal kit sold, along with cricket bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like cricket equipment but means crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A short evening gown is formal attire for a party.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: More old paintings were hung on the gallery wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ART into TRA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional or more is the adjectival sense, as in extra time.

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or disguised, so the letters are disguised by rearranging

explanation.surface: A tough cryptic crossword can be very annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean infuriating or annoying, close synonyms.

definitions.meaning: slimy garden molluscs that eat plants

explanation.surface: A gardener's drastic solution: shoot the pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a gun's rounds and garden molluscs share the word.

clue.text: Unfolding map, conclude it is simple

indicators.note: unfolding suggests opening out and rearranging, so the letters of the following words are reordered

explanation.surface: Opening up a map and deciding the route is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirteen letters of 'map, conclude it' are rearranged, signalled by 'Unfolding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple has no complications, a straightforward synonym.

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the planet's name is cut off

parts.note: Mars is the red planet

explanation.surface: An environmental complaint about ruining the Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final S of MARS.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or blemish it.

indicators.note: spread suggests scattering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Germs were spread close to a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a type of saw-billed diving duck, also called this.

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day; 'after dark' means at night
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A scary encounter involving a sinister black horse, or a racing outsider.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying ordeal is commonly called a bad dream come true.

parts.note: the Tate is a famous group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: Directions for a visitor: turn right just before the old gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve or spin round is the same as to turn.

clue.text: In Bognor, I'm in interesting seaside resort

indicators.note: In at the start says the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone in Bognor Regis, an English seaside town, says they are in an interesting resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across bognoR I'M IN Interesting; Bognor itself is a decoy resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a popular beach town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to voice an opinion is to say it

explanation.surface: A popular politician named Bill is asked to comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill for goods supplied is a commercial document requesting payment.

definitions.meaning: the base of the trunk left after felling
as a verb, to baffle someone

explanation.surface: A riddle about what is left of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the felled tree's base and to baffle someone share this word.

clue.text: Drew a stretch of land surrounded by Heath

indicators.note: surrounded by means the land word sits inside the name

parts.note: Ted Heath was a British Prime Minister, 1970-74
a tract is an area or stretch of land

explanation.surface: An artist sketched a piece of countryside ringed by heathland.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath is not moorland but Edward Heath, UK Prime Minister 1970-74, known by his short first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew in the sense of pulled in or lured, as a crowd is drawn.

indicators.note: various suggests different arrangements of the letters of items

explanation.surface: Assorted articles for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A self-reference: this crossword runs in that very newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is a long-established British daily newspaper.

clue.text: Potato, carrot, broccoli, spinach and cabbage — five, say

definitions.text: Potato, carrot, broccoli, spinach and cabbage

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
e.g. means 'for example', which 'say' also means

explanation.surface: A list of five vegetables, counted up at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'five' counts the list but gives V; 'say' gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: The listed items are all examples of vegetables, informally shortened.

parts.note: a top-level diplomatic meeting is jokingly pictured as one held on the world's highest peak

explanation.definitionFit: Talks between heads of government are named after a mountain's highest point.

clue.text: Food processor, where small vessel up-ended

indicators.note: in a down clue up-ended means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a tug is a small boat that tows ships

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget found where a little bowl was turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food processor' suggests a kitchen gadget, but means the body's digestive tract.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestines digest food, a witty description of the belly.

clue.text: Loop that's circling is coming up

indicators.note: circling means the loop goes round the next word

parts.note: a ring is a closed loop

explanation.surface: A loop that keeps going round is now on its way upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascending or going upward, like the sun at dawn.

parts.note: a scent is the trail a hound follows

explanation.surface: A hiker's simple instruction: climb a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb up a slope is a rise or upward journey, a noun synonym.
